rationale: DEVIL is defined exclusively as an HPV-independent, p53-wild-type verruciform/acanthotic squamous precursor of the vulva; it is not a recognized penile entity, restricting it to the vulvar subset of the code's ceiling.
As a generic 'differentiated intraepithelial neoplasia' term it is applied to both vulva (dVIN) and penis (dPeIN), covering essentially the full ceiling.
Differentiated (HPV-independent) PeIN is defined as a precursor lesion of the penis associated with male genital lichen sclerosus, restricting it to the penile subset of the code's ceiling.
Differentiated PeIN is by definition a penile intraepithelial neoplasia (HPV-independent precursor of penile SCC), restricting it to the penile subset of the code's ceiling.
dVIN is defined as the HPV-independent, TP53-mutant precursor of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma arising in vulvar lichen sclerosus, restricting it to the vulvar subset of the code's ceiling.
VAAD is defined as an uncommon HPV-independent squamous proliferation of the vulvar epithelium associated with vulvar verrucous carcinoma, restricting it to the vulvar subset of the code's ceiling.
By name and definition this is HPV-independent vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (dVIN/DEVIL/VAAD spectrum), restricting it to the vulvar subset of the code's ceiling.

Bowen disease (intraepidermal/in-situ squamous cell carcinoma) is a generic squamous in-situ lesion occurring across many cutaneous and mucosal sites; it is not restricted to a proper subset of the code's ceiling.

term: Intraepidermal squamous cell carcinoma, Bowen type
rationale: A generic descriptor for in-situ (intraepidermal) squamous cell carcinoma applicable across the many cutaneous/mucosal sites in the ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
Clear cell change is a generic morphologic pattern that can occur in squamous carcinomas at multiple anogenital and cutaneous sites; no literature restricts it to a proper subset of the ceiling.
A generic morphologic variant of squamous cell carcinoma defined by clear-cell change, occurring across multiple sites; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.

term: Squamous cell carcinoma, clear cell type
rationale: A generic morphologic descriptor of squamous cell carcinoma with clear-cell features; occurs at many sites and is not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.

WHO 5th ed. and the literature define adenoid basal carcinoma as a rare HPV-related epithelial neoplasm of the uterine cervix arising from cervical reserve cells, restricting it to the cervical subset of the code's ceiling.
Adenoid basal epithelioma is a WHO synonym for adenoid basal carcinoma, defined as a rare neoplasm of the uterine cervix, restricting it to the cervical subset of the code's ceiling.
source_name: International Journal of Clinical and Experimental Pathology (PMC)

rationale: This synonym for the indolent adenoid basal neoplasm is described exclusively as a cervical tumor derived from cervical reserve cells, restricting it to the cervical subset of the code's ceiling.

The code's ceiling already comprises only vulvar subsites; trichoblastic carcinoma is a follicular/adnexal skin malignancy that in this ceiling occurs in vulvar skin broadly, with no literature basis to restrict it below the vulvar subsites.
The ceiling is limited to vulvar subsites; this rare follicular adnexal tumor occurs in vulvar skin generally and no literature restricts it below those subsites.
A generic term for adenocarcinoma with mixed cell types applicable across the many organ sites in the ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
A generic descriptor for carcinoma composed of mixed cell types, applied across numerous sites; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
A generic mixed-cell adenocarcinoma descriptor applicable across many organ sites; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.

The code's ceiling is already limited to endometrium (C541) and uterus NOS (C549); atypical hyperplasia of the endometrium is an endometrial lesion covering essentially the full ceiling, so no proper subset can be established.

term: Endometrial atypical hyperplasia / endometrioid intraepithelial neoplasia
rationale: An endometrial precursor lesion; the ceiling is already only endometrium/uterus, so it covers essentially the full ceiling with no proper subset.
EIN is the endometrial precursor of endometrioid carcinoma; the ceiling is already only endometrium/uterus, so it covers essentially the full ceiling with no proper subset.

Endometrioid adenocarcinoma NOS occurs across multiple Mullerian and non-Mullerian sites in the ceiling (endometrium, ovary, cervix, fallopian tube, etc.); a generic term not restricted to a proper subset.
A generic term for endometrioid carcinoma applied at multiple sites (endometrium, ovary, cervix, tube); not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
A cystic endometrioid carcinoma pattern applicable to endometrioid carcinoma at multiple Mullerian sites (notably ovary); not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.

The MMRd molecular subgroup was developed for endometrial carcinoma but is also validated for ovarian endometrioid carcinoma, so it applies to more than one ceiling site and cannot be cleanly restricted to a defined proper subset.
The MMRd molecular classification applies to both endometrial and ovarian endometrioid carcinoma, spanning multiple ceiling sites without a clearly delimited proper subset.

term: No specific molecular profile (NSMP) endometrioid carcinoma
rationale: The NSMP subgroup of the TCGA/ProMisE molecular taxonomy applies to both endometrial and ovarian endometrioid carcinoma, so it spans multiple ceiling sites without a clearly delimited proper subset.

The POLE-ultramutated molecular subgroup was defined in endometrial carcinoma but also applies to ovarian endometrioid carcinoma, so it spans multiple ceiling sites without a clearly delimited proper subset.
POLEmut is part of the endometrial molecular taxonomy now also validated in ovarian endometrioid carcinoma, spanning multiple ceiling sites without a clearly delimited proper subset.
The p53-abnormal/TP53-mutant molecular subgroup applies to both endometrial and ovarian endometrioid carcinoma, spanning multiple ceiling sites without a clearly delimited proper subset.
The p53abn molecular subgroup applies to both endometrial and ovarian endometrioid carcinoma, spanning multiple ceiling sites without a clearly delimited proper subset.
The p53abn molecular subgroup is part of the endometrial taxonomy that also applies to ovarian endometrioid carcinoma, spanning multiple ceiling sites without a clearly delimited proper subset.

The secretory variant is described almost exclusively as an endometrial (uterine corpus) endometrioid carcinoma, but literature does not explicitly exclude ovarian/tubal endometrioid carcinoma, leaving the restriction ambiguous.
The ciliated cell variant of endometrioid adenocarcinoma is reported only as arising in the endometrium in all published cases, restricting it to the endometrial subset of the code's ceiling.

Endocervical-type adenocarcinoma is chiefly a cervical entity, but 'endocervical type' is also used as a Mullerian descriptor for vaginal adenocarcinoma (C529 is in the ceiling), so restriction to cervix alone is not clearly established.
source_name: American Journal of Surgical Pathology (PMC, IECC)

rationale: SEIC is defined as replacement of endometrial surface/glandular epithelium by serous carcinoma cells, i.e. the non-invasive precursor arising in the uterine corpus, restricting it to the endometrial/uterine subset (excluding ovary C569 and fallopian tube C570).
SEIC is by definition the endometrial serous intraepithelial precursor of uterine serous carcinoma, restricting it to the endometrial/uterine subset (excluding ovary and fallopian tube).
Unqualified 'serous intraepithelial carcinoma' encompasses both endometrial (SEIC) and tubal (STIC) forms, covering essentially the full ceiling and not restricted to a proper subset.

STIC is defined as the earliest morphologically recognizable serous carcinoma arising in the epithelium of the distal (fimbrial) fallopian tube, restricting it to the fallopian-tube subset of the code's ceiling.
The code's ceiling is only ovary (C569) and fallopian tube (C570); serous borderline tumors (including architectural variants) occur at both sites, covering the full ceiling with no proper subset.
Serous borderline tumors, including the micropapillary subtype, occur in both ovary and fallopian tube, which together comprise the full ceiling; no proper subset can be established.
The micropapillary variant of serous borderline tumor occurs at both ceiling sites (ovary and fallopian tube); not restricted to a proper subset.
Non-invasive low-grade serous (borderline) tumor occurs at both ceiling sites (ovary and fallopian tube); no basis to restrict it to a proper subset.
